headline: AI scientist Yann LeCun said he has no worry that AI will wipe out humanity and called Anthropic's Dario Amodei "deluded".
score_reason: The interview behind it was published on 2 Oct, before 4 Oct; lowered by 1.
importance_line: It shows a leading AI scientist rejecting the extinction arguments used to push regulation, but it is one researcher's opinion and he is building a competing company.
source: Fortune, as relayed by The Next Web
summary: The Next Web reports that Yann LeCun, a Turing Award winner who left Meta to found the AI start-up AMI Labs, told Fortune he does not worry "at all" about AI wiping out humanity and called Anthropic chief executive Dario Amodei "deluded". LeCun said recent rogue-AI incidents were preventable and blamed poor human oversight, and said he fears regulatory capture, meaning big firms shaping rules to shut out smaller rivals, more than extinction.
